title: Étale base-change arrows commute with restriction of coefficients
statement: Let Λ and Λ′ be commutative rings in Type(u+1), φ:Λ→Λ′ a ring homomorphism, and Y --e→ T, Y --h→ X, T --g→ S, X --p→ S a cartesian square of schemes [sbc-def-base-change-square], with g quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For every integer q and sheaf G of Λ′-modules on T_et, the degree-q base-change arrow [sbc-def-base-change-map] of the Λ-module sheaf Res_φ G is isomorphic in the arrow category of Λ-module sheaves on X_et to Res_φ applied to the degree-q base-change arrow of G.

source.place: Lemma 21.20.7(3), Tag 0D6J: coefficient-independent derived direct image; Remark 21.19.3, Tag 07A7: exchange via adjunction; assembled as the change-of-rings step of Coefficients.lean

proof.text: For a coefficient morphism φ:Λ→Λ′, restriction is exact and commutes with inverse image of module sheaves: both underlying inverse images and the restricted scalar actions agree. Direct image commutes with restriction sectionwise.

An injective Λ′-module sheaf is acyclic for direct image on each étale slice even after restricting coefficients. Compute higher direct images with such an injective resolution to get the canonical comparison of derived direct images. It is compatible with the derived-functor units and composition. This assertion concerns acyclicity, and does not assert that restriction preserves injective sheaves.

The underived exchange maps are mates under the pullback/direct-image adjunctions. The inverse-image and direct-image comparisons of step 1 identify their units and counits. Deriving and taking degree-q homology therefore gives commuting comparison maps on the source and target with the base-change maps. The vertical maps are isomorphisms by steps 1 and 2, giving an isomorphism in the arrow category. Negative degrees give zero endpoints.
